Again, this is a game about flying a spaceship around space with the final goal of defeating the flagship.

For anyone new to this game, definitely play on easy mode first so you can observe and learn the mechanics. It's easy to get overwhelmed, and there are things to notice that help you out big time, and if you miss them you will make things hard or impossible for yourself. Things like audio cues and "spaceship messages" that mean certain things.

I just beat the game on normal mode. Some things I learned along the way: it's always good to have rapid fire weapons to take down shields, however there are weapons that ignore or "pierce" shields, and, as I understand it, "pierce" means that it goes through shields without damaging them. There are tables you can use to look up which weapons do this, and I would look them up as you see them since it'll get overwhelming otherwise. From there I find it's nice to have a weapon that cause cause some chaos on board the other ship, like fires and breaches; this distracts the crew, and as you keep firing at the same location you can get more bang for your buck if you're killing crew members while attacking the part of the ship you want disabled. Sometimes it's good to shoot elsewhere in the ship, just to cause more problems elsewhere, and spread out their crew further.

Double ion cannons can get you through the entire game, you'll need something supplemental though for doing damage. Ion cannons can be used to suffocate the enemy by cutting off their oxygen supply, and when you kill all members on the ship you get a bonus with whatever loot you collect, and in my experience there's often a weapon sitting there, which can be sold for 17-50 scrap, and that's substantial.

As far a defense, upgrading your engines to dodge shots is far more useful than you might think, definitely put some points into that right away. Ironically, I found dodging, in combination with evasion, to be far more effective than shields. I guess you get to dodge lasers, ion blasts and missiles whereas shields only protects against lasers and ion blasts; and that carries a bonus of not experiencing the effects of ion blasts, since when the ion blast hits one's shields it does ion disable damage to the shields.

Defense drones are kind of like a better shield layer; they shoot down missiles, other drones (although sometimes I don't think they actively shoot at attacking drones, and I don't know why) and lasers (not sure about ion blasts, but I think it shoots those too). It's kind of expensive to acquire the drone apparatus (which enables use of drones) as well as the drones themselves, plus you have to pay for the system capacity power and the power bar to power it. Drones seem practical only for ships that come with the drone apparatus already installed, but I could be wrong.

Watch out for taking paths that will not let you get back to the exit before the rebel fleet reaches you, it happens enough to be on the look out for, and it can completely eff up a good run. If that happens to you, use the cheat engine program below to get back to where you were. The cheat engine can be a good tool for learning how the game plays as well.

Dual defense drones. Not defense II drones, just the first level. Your shields will soak up random laser fire, let 2 drones knock out 2 missiles and you're likely to dodge the 3rd or else deal with the single impact easily.
